gen-dafont-edo-sz-gf-carrois-gothic: Heavy, cast-iron swagger. Edo SZ draws its rounded, cord-like strokes at a constant width, while Carrois Gothic sits beside it with a tall, modern x-height and a lighter touch.
gen-dafont-edo-sz-gf-carrois-gothic-sc: Edo SZ has lowercase letters with the stature of cast iron capitals, drawn in a marker-nib line that ignores direction. And Carrois Gothic SC follows with clear openings at every curve's end, so its small letters stay close to its capitals.
gen-dafont-edo-sz-gf-chivo: Edo SZ bends thin steel rod into every letter. Chivo is the one to enjoy for its lowercase packed up toward the caps and its daylight through each curve, while the heading does the showing off.
gen-dafont-edo-sz-gf-chocolate-classical: Cultural and classic in feel, Edo SZ lays its line out like spaghetti, one constant stroke from letter to letter. Chocolate Classical Sans handles the reading, its broad-nibbed strokes never curling shut.
gen-dafont-edo-sz-gf-cossette-texte: Cossette Texte brings a prominent x-height and a wide-eyed lowercase e, clean and neutral on the page. Cossette Texte sits under Edo SZ, whose cast-iron-tall lowercase and constant stroke give the heading its classic, cultural weight.
gen-dafont-edo-sz-gf-duru-sans: Duru Sans reads wide and modern, its small letters opened up so the bodies dominate each line and the ascenders hardly show. But Edo SZ answers in cable-like strokes of one thickness, and the two feel like a monument beside a clean notice.
gen-dafont-edo-sz-gf-fresca: Chunky and cultural, Edo SZ holds a single constant stroke at the cast-iron height of capitals. Fresca takes over for reading, a plain sans with short ascenders above big bowls and apertures that stay connected to the outside.
gen-dafont-edo-sz-gf-funnel-sans: Funnel Sans reads crisp and professional, with tiny gaps between ascender tops and the x-height line and an e opened like a pried clasp. And its stroke widths stay put from stem to curve, so you can size it up a notch beneath Edo SZ.
gen-dafont-edo-sz-gf-gafata: Tube-like and sturdy, Edo SZ keeps one constant width through every stroke of its tall, cast-iron lowercase. But Gafata moves in a tall band of letters with short stalks above and wide-eyed e shapes, giving the heading a contemporary partner.
gen-dafont-edo-sz-gf-geist: Edo SZ gives its lowercase the stature of cast iron capitals, all in a single constant stroke. But Geist does the quiet work of making words read as solid blocks, with a level beat and no accents of weight.
